cases.purpose: Resolve independent cluster data into the exact attach and roam dry-run commands.
cases.script:
cluster=$HOME/cluster
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 700 "$cluster" || exit 1
printf 'node-1 parity@127.0.0.1:20861 /tmp/parity-home/fake-key\n' >"$cluster/members"
printf 'local-1\n' >"$cluster/node_id"
export BASHCLUSTER_STATE_DIR=$cluster
failed=0
mark() { if [[ $2 == 1 ]]; then printf '%s=PASS\n' "$1"; else printf '%s=FAIL\n' "$1"; failed=1; fi; }
screen attach node-1/work --remote --dry-run >"$HOME/attach-dry.txt" 2>"$HOME/attach-dry.err"; a=$?
screen roam node-1/work --dry-run >"$HOME/roam-dry.txt" 2>"$HOME/roam-dry.err"; b=$?
screen attach node-1/work --remote --dry-run --key /tmp/parity-home/override >"$HOME/attach-override.txt" 2>"$HOME/override.err"; c=$?
expected_attach=$'node=node-1\nsession=work\nhostport=parity@127.0.0.1:20861\nkey=/tmp/parity-home/fake-key\ncommand=screen attach work -r'
expected_roam=$'from=local-1\nto=node-1/work\nhostport=parity@127.0.0.1:20861\nkey=/tmp/parity-home/fake-key\ncommand=screen attach work -r'
expected_override=$'node=node-1\nsession=work\nhostport=parity@127.0.0.1:20861\nkey=/tmp/parity-home/override\ncommand=screen attach work -r'
good=0; [[ $a == 0 && $(<"$HOME/attach-dry.txt") == "$expected_attach" ]] && good=1; mark attach-command "$good"
good=0; [[ $b == 0 && $(<"$HOME/roam-dry.txt") == "$expected_roam" ]] && good=1; mark roam-command "$good"
good=0; [[ $c == 0 && $(<"$HOME/attach-override.txt") == "$expected_override" ]] && good=1; mark explicit-key-override "$good"
exit "$failed"
cases.oracle: The expected construction is a fixed literal derived from the documented dry-run contract and independent fixture cluster membership, with no transport connection.
cases.comparison: Compare the complete attach, roam and key override output and status.

cases.purpose: Round-trip independently encoded PTY, query, and control frames.
cases.script:
failed=0
mark() { if [[ $2 == 1 ]]; then printf '%s=PASS\n' "$1"; else printf '%s=FAIL\n' "$1"; failed=1; fi; }
root=$HOME/frames

for type in pty query control; do
  case $type in pty) payload='hi!';; query) payload='';; control) payload='resize 24 80';; esac
  screen remote-frame encode "$type" "$payload" >"$HOME/encoded-$type" 2>>"$HOME/frame-errors.log"; enc=$?
  screen remote-frame decode <"$HOME/encoded-$type" >"$HOME/decoded-$type" 2>>"$HOME/frame-errors.log"; dec=$?
  screen remote-frame decode <"$root/$type.frame" >"$HOME/independent-$type" 2>>"$HOME/frame-errors.log"; indep=$?
  good=0; [[ $enc == 0 && $dec == 0 && $indep == 0 ]] && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/$type.frame" "$HOME/encoded-$type" && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/$type.decoded" "$HOME/decoded-$type" && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/$type.decoded" "$HOME/independent-$type" && good=1
  mark "$type-roundtrip" "$good"
done
exit "$failed"
cases.oracle: Independent Python constructs BSCR magic, version, explicit type and big-endian lengths; expected decoded output is fixed without candidate results.
cases.comparison: Compare exact encoder bytes and both independently sourced and round-trip decoded bytes for all three frame types.

cases.purpose: Round-trip a valid frame at the 1 MiB payload boundary.
cases.script:
failed=0
mark() { if [[ $2 == 1 ]]; then printf '%s=PASS\n' "$1"; else printf '%s=FAIL\n' "$1"; failed=1; fi; }
root=$HOME/frames

payload=$(<"$root/maximum.payload")
screen remote-frame encode pty "$payload" >"$HOME/maximum-encoded" 2>"$HOME/maximum-encode.err"; enc=$?
screen remote-frame decode <"$root/maximum.frame" >"$HOME/maximum-decoded" 2>"$HOME/maximum-decode.err"; dec=$?
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/terra-local-pty-remote-r2.py frame-evidence "$enc" "$dec" || exit 1
good=0; [[ $enc == 0 && $dec == 0 ]] && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/maximum.frame" "$HOME/maximum-encoded" && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/maximum.decoded" "$HOME/maximum-decoded" && good=1
mark maximum-valid-frame "$good"
exit "$failed"
cases.oracle: The independent Python reference constructs a 1048576-byte payload, its big-endian length header and the complete expected decoder bytes.
cases.comparison: Byte-compare the entire 1 MiB encoder output and entire decoder output, including the exact boundary. Retain exact lengths, SHA-256 digests and first/last 16 bytes for expected and actual encoded/decoded files, plus statuses.

cases.purpose: Decode a valid BSCR payload containing NUL and a high-bit byte without losing data.
cases.script:
failed=0
mark() { if [[ $2 == 1 ]]; then printf '%s=PASS\n' "$1"; else printf '%s=FAIL\n' "$1"; failed=1; fi; }
root=$HOME/frames

screen remote-frame decode <"$root/binary.frame" >"$HOME/binary-decoded" 2>"$HOME/binary-decode.err"; rc=$?
good=0; [[ $rc == 0 ]] && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$root/binary.decoded" "$HOME/binary-decoded" && good=1
mark binary-payload-preserved "$good"
exit "$failed"
cases.oracle: Independent BSCR frame bytes contain A, NUL, FF, B; the expected decoder output explicitly includes all four bytes.
cases.comparison: Compare every byte including embedded NUL and high-bit data; a truncated string is a mismatch.

cases.purpose: Reject malformed or over-bound independently constructed BSCR frames.
cases.script:
failed=0
mark() { if [[ $2 == 1 ]]; then printf '%s=PASS\n' "$1"; else printf '%s=FAIL\n' "$1"; failed=1; fi; }
root=$HOME/frames

for name in short-header bad-magic bad-version bad-type short-payload over-limit; do
  screen remote-frame decode <"$root/$name.frame" >"$HOME/$name.out" 2>>"$HOME/malformed-errors.log"; rc=$?
  printf '%s %s\n' "$name" "$rc" >>"$HOME/malformed-status.log"
  good=0; [[ $rc != 0 && ! -s $HOME/$name.out ]] && good=1
  mark "$name-rejected" "$good"
done
exit "$failed"
cases.stdout:
short-header-rejected=PASS
bad-magic-rejected=PASS
bad-version-rejected=PASS
bad-type-rejected=PASS
short-payload-rejected=PASS
over-limit-rejected=PASS
cases.oracle: Independent Python creates explicit truncated headers, bad magic, invalid versions and types, a short payload, and a 1048577-byte declared length.
cases.comparison: Every malformed frame must return nonzero and produce no decoded output; each result is individually reported.
